living_cost.basis: Budget = official Student visa maintenance requirement outside London: GBP 1,203/month from 30 Nov 2026 (HC 584 raises it from the current GBP 1,171; 2027 applicants will fall under the new figure; the rate is reviewed yearly). London is GBP 1,570/month from 30 Nov 2026 (currently 1,529). Moderate (ESTIMATE) = University of Edinburgh single postgraduate estimate for 2026-27: GBP 1,542/month, GBP 18,504/year (accommodation and utilities 978, food and shopping 248, leisure 246, bus 58, phone 12; calculated March 2026). Comfortable (ESTIMATE) = Imperial College London 'Likely costs for living in London, 2026': GBP 1,821 (college-run accommodation) to 1,893 (private sector) per month; the upper figure is used. Imperial's own 25th-75th percentile range for 9 months is GBP 11,372-19,286. UCL, Manchester and LSE pages could not be read (403/503 errors), so no figure from them is used. Tuition, visa fees and the health surcharge are not included.

fees.label: Student visa application from outside the UK (main applicant; fee from 8 April 2026, unchanged in the 8 October 2026 table). The Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (GBP 55) is paid by the sponsor. The fee table lists no separate biometric enrolment fee; visa-application-centre service charges in India are not on the official fee table.

Immigration Health Surcharge for the extra 4 months of visa after the course ends (the visa runs 4 months past a course of 12 months or more; a part-year of 6 months or less is charged at half the yearly rate, so half of GBP 776). The full-course years are counted separately as health insurance.

proof_of_funds.text: Funds for living costs for up to 9 months: GBP 1,171/month (GBP 10,539) outside London or GBP 1,529/month (GBP 13,761) for London courses until 29 Nov 2026; from 30 Nov 2026 GBP 1,203 (GBP 10,827) outside London and GBP 1,570 (GBP 14,130) in London (HC 584). A master's of 9 months or longer counts the full 9 months. On top of that you must cover one academic year of course fees (up to 9 months) as stated on the CAS. Money must be held for 28 consecutive days, with the 28-day period ending within 31 days of the application date. Dependants: extra funds are required per family member, but a taught master's no longer qualifies for dependants (see work text and recent changes).

work_during_study.text: Home Office caseworker guidance: full-time degree-level students at a sponsor with a track record of compliance may work up to 20 hours a week in term time and full time in vacations; part-time courses carry no work right. Paid and voluntary work together count toward the cap. No self-employment, no professional sport/coaching and no public funds (gov.uk student visa pages). A taught master's does not allow dependants (courses starting on or after 1 Jan 2024; only research-based higher degrees or doctorates do). NOT CONFIRMED on 22 Oct 2026: the 20-hour figure comes from a summary of Home Office guidance, not from a gov.uk page we could read in full. Check it before relying on it.

post_study_work.name: Graduate visa (Graduate route)
post_study_work.text: A student starting a master's in 2026-27 or 2027 will graduate in 2027-28 and apply after 1 January 2027, so the shorter leave applies: 18 months for applications made on or after 1 Jan 2027 (24 months only for applications made on or before 31 Dec 2026; PhDs keep 3 years). Apply from inside the UK while holding a Student visa, after the university reports your course as completed. Fee GBP 937; health surcharge GBP 1,035 per year, so about GBP 1,552.50 for 18 months by the official part-year rule (the gov.uk cost page prints GBP 1,152.50 for 18 months, which does not match its own rule). No sponsor needed; most jobs and self-employment allowed; cannot be extended, only switched (e.g. to Skilled Worker).

pr_pathway.text: Main route: Skilled Worker visa, then settlement. Skilled Worker salary rules: general threshold GBP 41,700 or the occupation going rate, whichever is higher; recent graduates, people under 26 and those who held a Student or Graduate visa in the last 2 years can use GBP 33,400 and 70% of the going rate, for up to 4 years total stay. English for new Skilled Worker grants is B2 (from 8 Jan 2026). The gov.uk Skilled Worker page still says 5 years to settle, but the government proposes a 10-year baseline qualifying period (consultation closed 12 Feb 2026, outcome not published as of 22 Oct 2026) applying to people not yet settled; Graduate-route time does not count toward the 5-year routes; B2 English will be required for settlement applications from 26 Mar 2027. Skilled Worker visa fee (from outside the UK, 3 years or less) GBP 819, in the UK GBP 943.

recent_changes.title: Graduate route cut from 2 years to 18 months (PhD stays 3 years)
recent_changes.who_affected: Graduate visa applications made on or after 1 Jan 2027, so all students starting in 2026-27 or 2027 who are not on a doctorate
recent_changes.impact: Halves the time from 24 to 18 months to find a Skilled Worker job and sponsor; the home office modelled about 12,000 fewer student visa applications a year. For this country's master's students the 18-month figure is the planning case.

recent_changes.title: Student maintenance funds rise to GBP 1,570 (London) and GBP 1,203 (outside London) per month
recent_changes.who_affected: Student visa applications decided under the rules from 30 Nov 2026, including all 2027 entrants
recent_changes.impact: Up 41 (London) and 32 (elsewhere) per month, so 9 months of funds goes to GBP 14,130 or GBP 10,827 plus first-year course fees; the family must arrange slightly more cash or loan before applying. Accommodation offset maximum also rises.

check.note: The amounts come from the HC 584 text (ST 12.3 and 12.4: 1529 to 1570, 1171 to 1203); the page does not label which figure is London, which is inferred from the current GBP 1,529 London rate on gov.uk.

recent_changes.title: International student levy of GBP 925 per student per year on English universities
recent_changes.who_affected: English higher education providers, from academic year 2028-29 (first 220 students per provider exempt); not charged to students directly
recent_changes.impact: Falls after a 2026-27/2027 master's cohort finishes, so no direct cost for them, but universities may raise fees for later years. Draft Finance Bill clause published 13 Jul 2026; not yet law.

check.note: The 220-student allowance and inflation uprating come from secondary reporting of the policy; the gov.uk page read gives rate, start date, who pays and draft status. Passing the cost on to students is not addressed.

recent_changes.title: Dependants barred for taught postgraduate students
recent_changes.who_affected: Students on taught master's courses starting on or after 1 Jan 2024 (research degrees and doctorates still allowed)
recent_changes.impact: No partner or children can accompany a taught-master's student, which removes a second income and family-visa cost but also the option of bringing family.

recent_changes.title: Stricter sponsor compliance thresholds (BCA) for universities
recent_changes.who_affected: Universities applying for or keeping a student sponsor licence; students at weaker institutions
recent_changes.impact: Refusal rate must be under 5% (was 10%), enrolment at least 95% (was 90%), completion 85% rising to 90% from 1 Jun 2027. Universities with many refusals may lose recruitment ability, so pick well-established providers. Indian refusal rates matter for institutions with large Indian intakes.

recent_changes.title: Student visa fee raised from GBP 524 to GBP 558; Graduate visa fee from GBP 880 to GBP 937
recent_changes.who_affected: All Student visa applicants from outside the UK and Graduate visa applicants
recent_changes.impact: Adds GBP 34 to the student visa and GBP 57 to the Graduate visa versus 2025. The 8 Oct 2026 table shows no change; April 2027 changes are possible.

recent_changes.title: English requirement for new Skilled Worker grants raised to B2; B2 for settlement from 26 March 2027
recent_changes.who_affected: People switching from Graduate to Skilled Worker (initial grants), and Skilled Worker applicants for settlement from 26 Mar 2027
recent_changes.impact: Graduates of English-taught UK degrees can usually meet B2 easily; the later settlement requirement is higher than before (B1).

recent_changes.title: Earned settlement: 10-year baseline qualifying period proposed
recent_changes.who_affected: Skilled Worker and other route holders who have not yet received indefinite leave to remain, including future Graduate-to-Skilled-Worker switchers
recent_changes.impact: Could double the wait for permanent residence from 5 to 10 years, with reductions for high earners (5 years off above GBP 50,270 for 3 years, 7 years off above GBP 125,140). Low-skilled roles could face 15 years. Graduate-route time would not count toward the 5-year routes.

check.note: The official consultation page (closed 12 Feb 2026) says the outcome is not yet published as of 22 Oct 2026; a law-firm note (secondary) says policy is due before end-2026. Final rules and transitional arrangements are unknown.

recent_changes.title: Skilled Worker salary thresholds: GBP 41,700 general, GBP 33,400 for new entrants
recent_changes.who_affected: Graduates switching to Skilled Worker; sponsors
recent_changes.impact: A typical graduate salary may fall below GBP 41,700 but can still qualify under the new-entrant route (GBP 33,400 and 70% of the going rate) for up to 4 years in total, including time on the Graduate visa.

check.note: Figures read on the gov.uk Skilled Worker pages; the 22 July 2025 effective date comes from a search summary of HC 997 and the Home Office impact assessment, not from a page opened in full.

policy_volatility.evidence: In the last 24 months the UK ended dependants for taught master's (Jan 2024), raised fees (Apr 2026), tightened sponsor compliance (Jun 2026), announced the Graduate route cut (effective Jan 2027), an international student levy (Aug 2028), an annual maintenance uplift (30 Nov 2026) and consulted on doubling the settlement qualifying period. Nearly every route element has been changed or proposed for change.

psw_uncertainty.evidence: Graduate visa shrinks to 18 months for applications from 1 Jan 2027 and cannot be extended. Conversion needs a sponsored Skilled Worker job at GBP 41,700 (or GBP 33,400 and 70% of the going rate for new entrants, 4-year cap) while entry pay for 22-29 year olds in science/tech professions is a median of about GBP 40,016 (ASHE 2026 provisional). Settlement timing may move from 5 to 10 years (proposal, outcome unpublished).

work_restrictions.evidence: Up to 20 hours a week in term time and full time in vacations for degree-level study (caseworker guidance), no self-employment; no work right for part-time courses; no dependants on taught master's. The Graduate visa is fully open (most jobs and self-employment).

funds_burden.evidence: Must show GBP 10,827 (outside London) to GBP 14,130 (London) from 30 Nov 2026 for 9 months, held 28 consecutive days, plus one academic year of course fees (up to 9 months) per the CAS, plus visa GBP 558 and health surcharge (GBP 776 per year, about GBP 1,164 for a 16-month visa). Large but somewhat shorter and more predictable than a blocked account.

recent_adverse.evidence: Last 12 months: Graduate cut to 18 months laid in Oct 2025, GBP 34 fee rise in Apr 2026, tougher sponsor thresholds Jun 2026, maintenance rises again from 30 Nov 2026, levy draft law Jul 2026, Skilled Worker B2 English and the open settlement consultation. No loosening for students.

CS.basis: ONS ASHE 2026 (provisional, April 2026 reference, published 22 Oct 2026), Table 20.7a 'Age group by occupation (2-digit SOC 2020): Annual pay - Gross', sheet Full-Time, UK, age 22-29, SOC 21 'Science, research, engineering and technology professionals' (includes IT professionals but also engineers and scientists; 274k jobs). Low = 25th percentile 32,649; mid = median 40,016; high = 75th percentile 51,089. No 4-digit SOC split by age exists. Caveat: 22-29s include first-degree entrants and non-London jobs, so a UK master's graduate in London may earn more. Cross-check, all ages, full-time, Table 14.7a SOC 2134 Programmers and software development professionals: 25th 43,509, median 59,863, 75th 82,149.

tax.basis: ESTIMATE, computed by us for a single employee in England, Wales or Northern Ireland on the CS entry_mid salary of GBP 40,016, tax year 2026-27, from HMRC/gov.uk rates: Personal Allowance GBP 12,570 and 20% basic rate to GBP 50,270; employee Class 1 National Insurance (category A) 8% between GBP 12,570 and GBP 50,270 (2% above). Taxable pay 40,016 - 12,570 = 27,446. Income tax 20% x 27,446 = 5,489; NI 8% x 27,446 = 2,196; total 7,685 / 40,016 = 19.2%. Excludes Scottish bands, pension auto-enrolment, student loan repayments, and the Immigration Health Surcharge (already paid in the visa). Rate on the DS entry_mid is the same; on the MBA mid (52,295) it is about 21%.

health_insurance_per_year.basis: Immigration Health Surcharge, student rate (students and their dependants, GBP 776 per year; adult rate GBP 1,035). Paid up front with the visa application; a visa longer than one year is charged the yearly cost plus half the yearly cost if the extra is 18 months or less in total, so a typical 16-month visa for a 12-month master's costs about GBP 1,164. Gives NHS access. Fixed official charge, not an estimate.

checklist: Get an offer from a licensed student sponsor and wait for your Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS); you cannot apply for the visa without it, and you can apply up to 6 months before the course starts.

Check with your university whether your course needs an ATAS certificate (mainly some postgraduate subjects for non-UK/non-exempt nationals such as Indians); it is free but takes at least 30 working days, so apply early.
Prove English at CEFR B2: a Secure English Language Test (SELT), an Ecctis-confirmed English-taught degree, or an assessment by your university.

Arrange funds: living costs for 9 months (GBP 10,539 outside London / 13,761 London now; GBP 10,827 / 14,130 from 30 Nov 2026) plus the first-year course fee on your CAS, held in your or your parents' account for 28 consecutive days ending within 31 days of applying.
Take a tuberculosis (TB) test at an approved clinic in India (India is on the UKVI list; the certificate is valid for 6 months from the x-ray) and include the certificate with your application.

Apply online, pay the GBP 558 visa fee and the Immigration Health Surcharge (GBP 776 per year, about GBP 1,164 for 16 months), then give biometrics and upload documents at the visa application centre.
During study work no more than 20 hours a week in term (check your visa conditions), no self-employment, and note that dependants cannot join you on a taught master's.

After graduating apply for the Graduate visa (GBP 937 plus health surcharge) from inside the UK before your Student visa expires; for applications from 1 Jan 2027 it lasts 18 months, so start job hunting early.
